title: Contraction of associated primes of a fractional monogenic principal quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $K$ its fraction field, and $x\in K$ nonzero. Assume $S=R[x]$ is Noetherian, and let $m$ be a maximal ideal of $S$ containing $x$. Put $A=S_m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $t=x/1$. If $p$ is an associated prime of $A/tA$, meaning the annihilator of a nonzero class is $p$, then its contraction to $R$ is an associated prime of $R/J$, where $J=R\cap xR$.

source.place: Tag 0334, Step 5, paragraphs identifying S/xS = R/(R ∩ xR) and verifying (2), (3)(a); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0334

proof.text: The shared adjoin quotient-surjectivity theorem proves that the map R → S/xS is surjective: the generator maps to zero, and constants, sums and products lift.

To identify its kernel J, write r = x f(x). If r = 0 there is nothing to prove. Otherwise P = C r - X f vanishes at x, and reverse(P) vanishes at x inverse with leading coefficient r. The leading-coefficient integrality lemma gives that r/x is integral over R, and normality puts it in R. Conversely r = cx with c in R belongs to xS. The first isomorphism theorem gives R/J ≃ S/xS.

The module A/tA is the localization of S/xS at m. Mathlib Module.associatedPrimes.comap_mem_associatedPrimes_of_mem_associatedPrimes_of_isLocalizedModule_of_fg contracts p to an associated prime qS of S/xS, using Noetherianity of S.

Choose an annihilator witness for qS. Its annihilator over R is the contraction qS ∩ R by the scalar-tower identity. Transport this witness through the R-linear isomorphism R/J ≃ S/xS; its annihilator is unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Identify the quotient kernel by reversing C r - X f and applying leading-coefficient integrality; contract an associated prime of the localized finite quotient, then restrict and transport its annihilator witness.
